name: Citizenship by Naturalisation (Standard Route)

requirements.blocker_text: 5 years of uninterrupted legal residence in Ukraine (reduced to 3 years for refugees, stateless persons, and certain categories of military service members).
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years of continuous legal residence in Ukraine.

requirements.blocker_text: Demonstrated knowledge of the fundamentals of Ukraine's Constitution and history, and state-language proficiency, per standards set by the National Commission on State Language Standards.
Lawful means of subsistence (not required for refugees, military personnel, or those with special-merit status).
Written declaration recognising and committing to observe Ukraine's Constitution and laws.

A renunciation declaration or a commitment to terminate foreign citizenship is generally required, though simplified declaration-based procedures now exist for specific categories under the new multiple-citizenship framework (see ua_citizenship_dual_declaration.json).

evidence_required.document: Proof of 5 years' continuous legal residence (3 years for refugees/stateless/certain military)
Constitution, history, and state-language exam pass
Proof of lawful means of subsistence
Written declaration of allegiance to the Constitution and laws
Renunciation declaration or foreign-citizenship termination commitment

sources.title: State Migration Service of Ukraine -- Admission to Ukrainian Citizenship: 5-year continuous residence (3 years for refugees, stateless persons, certain military categories), Constitution/history/language exam, lawful means of subsistence, allegiance declaration, foreign-citizenship renunciation, with preferential consideration for spouses married 3+ years to a Ukrainian citizen, refugees, military service, and persons of distinguished merit

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ukraine). dual_citizenship_allowed is false for THIS standard route since renunciation/termination of foreign citizenship remains the general default rule -- see ua_citizenship_dual_declaration.json for the new Article 5-1 framework (effective 16 January 2026) that allows specific groups (citizens of Poland, Czech Republic, Germany, Canada, and the USA via simplified declaration; and military-connected families) to retain foreign citizenship. This is a live, very recently reformed area of Ukrainian law -- the core 5-year/exam/means figures quoted here come directly from dmsu.gov.ua and were not contradicted by any other source found, unlike Peru's or Vietnam's citizenship-law transitions elsewhere in this dataset, so this file is published without a live-transition caveat.
